claims.meaning: Public MHS preview material supports standardized device discovery/state/read-write/orchestration and declared device characteristics/safety limits; Universal Robots separately keeps underlying robot safety architecture in charge.
allowedWording: MHS standardizes an agent-facing hardware integration layer
declared MHS bounds do not replace every underlying machine safety mechanism
avoid: MHS replaces certified robot safety systems

claims.meaning: The Genentech foaming episode shows that an operable interface and runtime feedback can coexist with an incorrect physical diagnosis; expert physical interpretation changed the corrective action.
allowedWording: successful device access does not establish correct physical-state interpretation

claims.meaning: NIST guidance treats metrological traceability, when applicable, as a property of a particular measurement result and states that traceability alone does not guarantee fitness for purpose; instrument identity/calibration alone is insufficient to establish result adequacy for a declared use.
allowedWording: device readability is not itself measurement adequacy
traceability where required still does not by itself establish fitness for purpose
measurement adequacy depends on the declared use, uncertainty, method and conditions
avoid: every agent measurement requires metrological traceability

claims.meaning: QuEra owner-primary evidence shows agent-derived laser settings were checked with an independent out-of-loop measurement and long-horizon behavior; NASA V&V supplies a mature engineering analogue for separating conformance evidence from intended-use validation.
allowedWording: operation or proxy success need not settle the stronger intended-use claim
verification and intended-use validation are distinct engineering questions
avoid: one validation pattern is universal across science
the MHS interface owns downstream result/use admission

claims.meaning: A scoped synthesis of MHS/UR/QuEra cases, LAP prior art and mature NIST/NASA references separates agent-hardware operability, native safety, physical diagnosis, measurement adequacy and intended-use evidence sufficiency. These are distinct questions/contracts, not a required sequential pipeline or five-service architecture.
allowedWording: ask which question has actually been established
the questions may have different evidence owners
passing one question does not grant the others
avoid: the five questions are an MHS specification
this is a novel universal ontology of physical AI
